ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper structure in the figure contains a negatively charged oxygen, located above the carbonyl position connected to OR¹; this oxygen has a curved arrow pointing to the upper carbonyl carbon, indicating re-formation of C=O. On the left there is an R-substituted alkene fragment connected to this carbonyl carbon, and another curved arrow points from the alkene π bond to the lower carbonyl carbon. The lower carbonyl carbon is connected to R² and OR³, and there is a curved arrow from the lower C=O π bond pushed toward oxygen. Reasoning: according to the method set in the question, map R, R¹, R², R³ all to [*]. After the action of the three arrows, the upper part becomes an ester carbonyl C(=O)O[*]; the alkene carbon and the lower carbonyl carbon form a new C–C bond; the lower carbonyl becomes a tetrahedral carbon, connected to O, O[*], R², and the newly formed C–C bond. Therefore the product skeleton is R²-C(O)(OR³)-C(R)-C(=O)OR¹, corresponding to the SMILES [*]C(O)(C([*])C(O[*])=O)O[*].

method.method_draft: Map R, R1, R2, and R3 in the drawing to four [*] substituents. Apply the three curved arrows: make the upper carbonyl C(=O)O[*], connect the alkene carbon bearing R to the lower carbonyl carbon, and convert the lower C=O into a tetrahedral carbon bearing O, O[*], R2, and the new C–C bond. Encode the resulting skeleton R2-C(O)(OR3)-C(R)-C(=O)OR1 as the SMILES [*]C(O)(C([*])C(O[*])=O)O[*].
